target_customer: Energy retailers, utilities, EV charging and smart home companies that need to connect to and control consumer energy devices
problem: Every EV, charger, battery and thermostat has its own proprietary interface; Enode offers one API to connect and optimize them for energy products and grid flexibility.
business_model: B2B API platform, usage and per device pricing
product_category: Energy device connectivity API and orchestration

founders.name: Henrik Langeland
founders.background_notes: YC page lists role only; backgrounds not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Nikolai Heum
founders.background_notes: YC page lists co-founder; CTO title from search results on the company about page, not opened.

competitors.name: Smartcar
competitors.what: Connected car API for electric, hybrid and conventional vehicles

competitors.name: High Mobility
competitors.what: Car data API with standardized vehicle data points, maintained since 2014

technical_complexity.rationale: Reverse engineering and maintaining many vendor APIs and normalizing them is steady engineering work, not research, but reliability and device coverage are hard to sustain.

defensibility.rationale: Broad device coverage and customer integrations build up over time, but connector approaches are replicable and vendors can open official APIs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Connected car API vendors existed; no source shows an acquisition or copying of Enode, and it expanded into home energy and flexibility.

market_need_then: Energy retailers needed to offer smart charging and flexibility as EVs and home batteries spread, and the energy transition drove investor interest shown by the seed and Series A.

identity.voice_and_tone: Infrastructure and developer oriented, described as the Plaid for energy in one source; tagline 'Orchestrating energy for the next grid'

brand_strength.rationale: Short invented name with a clear positioning line, but no press or community evidence about the brand itself.

pivots.from: API for connecting EVs and energy devices
pivots.to: Energy orchestration platform for retailers (device connectivity, home coordination, grid flexibility)
pivots.why: Seen in YC page tagline and site positioning; timing and reasons not sourced.

outcome_analysis: Enode raised a $2.2M seed in July 2021 and a $15M Series A led by Creandum in November 2022, and grew to about 70 people with customers such as Vattenfall. The shift to electrification and flexible demand created a need for a unified device layer, and the company moved from an EV API to a broader energy orchestration platform. Competitors in connected car APIs existed, so breadth beyond cars was the key differentiator.
notes: Seed is stated by one outlet page; a second outlet snippet (Mainsights) reports NOK 19M which is consistent in size but was not opened. eu-startups reported the Series A as EUR 15M while the company blog and tech.eu say $15M. Aggregators total $17.1M to $17.4M, consistent with the two rounds. Smartcar's page is vendor authored and compares Smartcar features as of September 2021. High Mobility source is undated; competitor existence before the batch is supported by its 'maintained since 2014' description. Third founder Thorvald Thorsnes appears only in aggregator listings and is not recorded.
